description: Where the hand model stands against published data, step by step. 'quantities' holds the literature values (with spread, source and protocol); 'steps' holds the model values recorded by scripts/hand_literature_comparison.py after each change of the hand. docs/wiki/hand-literature-comparison.md is generated from this file. Literature values are cited, never copied from figures: each row names the table it comes from.

mcfarland2023.note: Protocols and results of its ARMS model are cited only; no ARMS file, parameter or coordinate is used.

steps.title: Step 1: hand models derived from the arm by generic pruning
steps.summary: No arm model changes (every MjModel array of myoarm_r, myoarms, myotorso_arms and myofullbody is identical before and after). myohand_r and myohands are the arm pruned; their actuators, tendons, equalities and pairs equal the arm's. This is the baseline of the rebuild, measured on myoarm_r.
notes: The grip is a fresh optimisation on this commit (balanced wrist, four restarts); its digit shares differ from the cached optimum in hand-function-validation.md (30 / 37 / 25 / 8 %) by up to 14 points.
No contact pair of myoarm_r involves a finger: in the active fist the fingers pass into the palm geoms and each other (negative fingertip-to-palm distances).

Fingertip values re-measured with the method of S1 (palmar direction from the long flexor, D_N0 at the distal palmar corner); the first recording measured along the old pads' normals, which point dorsally (see S1).

steps.title: S0: side suffix on every right-arm name
steps.summary: Names only. scripts/compare_model_numerics.py finds every MjModel array, and the tendon lengths, actuator lengths and moments, passive forces and body positions at five random postures, identical to step 1 in myohand_r, myohands, myoarm_r, myoarms, myotorso_arms, myofullbody and both hand fragments. The hand-function protocols rerun on the renamed model give the same numbers to the last printed digit, so the model stands where it stood after step 1.
notes: Fingertip values re-measured with the method of S1 (palmar direction from the long flexor, D_N0 at the distal palmar corner); the first recording measured along the old pads' normals, which point dorsally (see S1).

steps.title: S1: hand self-contacts and pads
steps.summary: Fingertip pads moved to the palmar side and fitted to Dallard's D_N0 (6.4 mm, scaled by distal-phalanx length); palm, thenar and hypothenar pads; 144 self-contact pairs per hand in one shared file used by every model with a hand. Before = S0 with the same validation scenes (the scenes now remove the model's own contact pairs, as the protocol states).
notes: Grip: the dynamometer is moved palmarly until it touches the palm, which is now the 19 mm palm pad instead of the metacarpal capsules; the dynamometer sits 11 mm further palmar, so the hand closes on it wider open. The self-selected grip falls below the in-vivo band (O'Driscoll 1992 mean - 1 SD = 270.7 N) and the digit shares move to within 4 points of the ARMS shares.

Active fist: digits 2, 4 and 5 touch the palm and hypothenar pads (within 0.8 mm); digit 3 stops 18 mm short, held by its neighbours (with MCP abduction free the flexing fingers converge). Penetration beyond each pair's margin stays below 1 mm.

The palm pad thickness (19.1 mm) comes from the fist criterion with the joints at their flexion limits; the model's PIP limit (90 deg) is below the usual 100-110 deg, so the fingertips land farther from the bones than in a real fist and the pad compensates.

Tenodesis and lateral pinch are unchanged: their scenes remove all model contact pairs (the protocol). With the self-contacts kept, tenodesis with MCP abduction locked fails the direction check (largest reversal 2.6 deg against 2 deg): fingers 2-4 converge and push each other.

steps.title: S1b: PIP flexion range from the literature
steps.summary: PIP flexion limit of digits 2-5 raised from 90 to 115 deg (Leijnse et al. 2010, maximum passive flexion, 115 +- 7 deg); palm pads refitted to the fist at the new limits; the PIP springs refitted (they change by less than 0.01 %); EDM loses a wrap that switched on abruptly near PIP5 108 deg. Before = S1.
notes: Grip: with the 8.0 mm palm pad (was 19.1 mm) the dynamometer sits closer to the metacarpals and the fingers close further around it. The self-selected grip rises from 232.5 to 310.3 N, back inside the in-vivo band (O'Driscoll 1992 mean - 1 SD = 270.7 N), and the settled grip from 132.8 to 282.9 N. The digit shares (29.5 / 38.0 / 22.9 / 9.5 %) are within 6 points of the ARMS shares.
Active fist: digits 2, 4 and 5 touch the palm and hypothenar pads; digit 3 still stops short, now 14.4 mm (was 18.5 mm), held by its neighbours.

Palm pad: 8.0 mm with the fingertips at the new flexion limits, close to the hypothenar muscle thickness of Misirlioglu (8.4 +- 1.9 mm); the hypothenar pad changes little (16.8 mm), as digit 5 lands on it with MCP and DIP, not PIP, setting the reach.
Tenodesis passes all checks; trial A ROM of digit 5 PIP is 80 deg, the other values move by at most 2 deg. Lateral pinch is unchanged (no thumb change).

Passive PIP moment near the new end range (muscles at act = 0 plus springs, other joints at 0): index -0.08 / -0.11 / -0.14 N m at 90 / 100 / 115 deg, digits 3-4 -0.07 to -0.10 N m; Kamper 2002 measured up to 60 deg (held at -0.04 N m beyond). The excess over the held value comes from the interosseous and lumbrical bundles stretched over the PIP (LU_RB, UI_UB), which a restoring spring cannot remove. Digit 5: -0.16 / -0.24 N m at 90 / 100 deg, but LU_RB5 turns into a PIP flexor at 114-115 deg (its wrap over Fifthpm_wrap_r switches side), so the total becomes +0.16 N m at the limit; the lumbrical paths are rebuilt in S5.

steps.title: S2: thumb and first-dorsal-interosseous heads, opponens fix
steps.summary: AdP split into AdPt and AdPo (Stamenkovic 2014 head ratio of Jacobson's PCSA), FPB into FPBs and FPBd and the first dorsal interosseous (RI2) into DI1s and DI1d (Mirakhorlo 2016 head ratios); one generalised intrinsic table and generator; OP, APB, the FPB heads and the DI1 heads fitted to published moment arms (Smutz 1998; An 1983), the AdP heads on their registered Mirakhorlo 2016 paths; passive scales of the thumb intrinsics fitted to the measured passive totals and the springs refitted. Before = S1b; the before columns of the moment arms are AdP, FPB and RI2 of S1b.
notes: Thumb CMC kinematics: with MyoHand's CMC axes no site shift reproduces Smutz's abduction trends: OP, AdP and FPB grow more adductor toward adduction in the model and more abductor in Smutz's specimens. The fits match the neutral values within one SD where reachable; the OP abduction arm stays at -2.4 mm (Smutz -4.8 +- 5.0).

AdP heads: fitted to Smutz's flexion arms they lose their adduction arm, and the lateral pinch then has no solution within its off-axis limit (best 20.5 N at 1.9 x off-axis). They keep the registered Mirakhorlo paths instead (moved only to keep AdPt below 1.6 normalised fibre length over the full thumb range): CMC flexion 19.4 / 14.7 mm (Smutz 36.9 / 27.0), adduction 16.8 / 1.4 mm (20.6 / 17.0).
Lateral pinch 38.7 -> 52.9 N, at the in-vivo mean (Valero-Cuevas 2003, 51.9 +- 20.4 N); below Mathiowetz's key pinch (women 72.1 +- 13.3 N, men 109.0 +- 20.5 N), as for the ARMS model.

Index MCP abduction moment with both DI1 heads active: 0.34 -> 1.05 N m (force 61.2 -> 129.4 N at the thenar precedent of 86.3 N/cm2, moment arm 5.6 -> 8.1 mm), equal to Infantolino & Challis's in-vivo FDI moment (about 1.0 N m) and 39-57 % of the RIHM norms.

Passive thumb moments: the passive scale (fpmax) of OP, AdPo and the FPB heads fits to near zero, AdPt 0.69, APB 0.44 (MuJoCo's curve is much stiffer than measured ones, as for the extrinsic muscles). Spring fits (RMS against the source): thumb CMC flexion 0.074 -> 0.009 N m, CMC abduction 0.128 -> 0.075 N m, MP 0.028 -> 0.010 N m (the MP excess of FPB and AdP is gone).
Grip: the intrinsics are inactive in the grip, but their passive forces change; self-selected grip 310.3 -> 334.8 N, settled 305.9 N. Tenodesis passes unchanged.

steps.title: S3: fourth and fifth carpometacarpal joints
steps.summary: CMC4 and CMC5 hinges (centres sphere-fitted to the metacarpal bases; CMC5 axis from Shimawaki 2019, CMC4 on the CMC5 pattern), coupled CMC5 = 2.06 x CMC4 by a joint equality; ranges -5 to 16 and -10.3 to 33 deg; the digit-5 flexor via points and three interosseous origins moved so that only the anatomical crossings remain (paths unchanged at CMC 0); linear end-range springs from El-Shennawy 2001's load. Before = S2.
notes: Crossing moment arms (dL/dq at 0, CMC4 / CMC5, mm): FDS4 -6.0 / -, FDP4 -3.3 / -, EDC4 13.1 / -, FDS5 - / -9.3, FDP5 - / -6.4, EDC5 - / 10.0, EDM - / 7.4, ECU - / 3.5, FCU - / -4.6, LU_RB4 -8.8 / -, UI_UB5 - / -3.6. Before the site moves FDP5 would have flexed CMC4 (16.9) and extended CMC5 (10.7), and RI5 extended CMC5 (7.1).

Coupling: 2.06 is the ratio of the mean active maxima of one cohort (CMC5 25.1 +- 3.5, CMC4 12.2 +- 3.0 deg); individual ratios are not reported and vary at least as much as these SDs (14 % and 25 % of the means). Passive end-range arcs bound the ratio at about 2.2-2.75 (El-Shennawy 2001); Buffi 2013's single subject gives 2.72. With CMC4 pinned CMC5 still moves 28 +- 3 deg in cadaver tests, which the equality cannot reproduce.

Ranges: the arcs match El-Shennawy's passive arcs; the split into flexion and extension is assumed (Aljasim 2025 finds more extension than flexion from the MC3 axis under 100 N). The active maxima lie 3.8 / 7.9 deg inside the flexion limits.
Relaxed hand: without springs the muscles' passive tension (mostly FDP5) cupped the hand to 10 / 21 deg; with the end-range springs it rests within 0.2 deg of neutral.

Grip: 334.8 -> 314.9 N, digit-5 share 9.9 -> 12.0 % (ARMS 11.5 %), settled 305.9 -> 278.0 N; the active fist leaves the middle finger 16.3 mm from the palm (14.4 before). Tenodesis and lateral pinch unchanged.

steps.title: S4: hypothenar muscles
steps.summary: UI_UB5 re-routed as ADM (pisiform to the ulnar base of the proximal phalanx, via point on the MC5 head, fitted to An 1979's little-finger moment potentials); FDM and ODM added on their registered Mirakhorlo 2016 paths; Jacobson 1992 architecture at the thenar specific tension (ADM 76.8 N, was 47.9 N; FDM 46.6 N; ODM 94.9 N); passive scales and springs refitted. Before = S3; the before columns of ADM are UI_UB5.
notes: ADM no longer reaches the lateral band (Santo Neto 1984: an aponeurosis expansion in 16 % of hands), so it has no PIP moment (UI_UB5: 2.8 mm extensor). In tenodesis the little-finger PIP range falls from 80 to 40 deg and the largest index-to-other-digit PIP spread from 82 to 37 deg (ARMS: 16 and 15 deg).
Little-finger abduction: ADM and FDM give 1.02 N m at rest (UI_UB5 0.32 N m), between the RIHM norms of women (0.95) and men (1.56 N m), at the thenar specific tension of 86.3 N/cm2.
Active cupping with ODM, FDM and ADM: CMC4 / CMC5 11.4 / 23.6 deg, inside the in-vivo maxima of maximal little-finger opposition (12.2 +- 3.0 / 25.1 +- 3.5 deg).

Grip 314.9 -> 377.2 N with the digit-5 share 12.0 -> 20.6 % (ARMS 11.5 %; within the protocol's 12-point tolerance); settled 278.0 -> 339.7 N. FDM and ODM are not in the grip's muscle set; the change comes from their passive tension and ADM's path. Lateral pinch unchanged (52.9 N).
FDM and ODM have no published moment arms: their registered paths are kept and checked for sign (both flex CMC5; FDM flexes and ulnarly abducts MCP5: 6.4 / 5.3 mm).

steps.title: EM-a: finger extensor mechanism (option a) and oblique retinacular ligament
steps.summary: EDC2-5, EIP, EDM, LU_RB2-5 and UI_UB2-4 end on junction sites of the proximal phalanx and branch (MuJoCo pulleys) into the central slip and the lateral bands to the terminal tendon: extensors c (1 - r) / c r with r = 0.63 (Lee 2008a) and c = 1.0 fitted to the index IP moment arms (An 1983; Lee 2008b), intrinsics after Chao & An 1978 (via Brook 1995). One tension-only ORL per finger, slack while DIP - PIP <= 30 deg (Harris & Rutledge 1972), stiffness from Ueba 2011 at PIP 0. Extrinsic slack lengths and passive scales and the joint springs refitted. Before = S4 (the extension columns of S4 are measured on the S4 model).
notes: Extensor share c = 1.0 (unbounded optimum 1.09; RMS z 0.34 over An 1983 and Lee 2008b for EDC2 and EIP), against Lee 2008a's nine-posture mean of 0.39 (0.72 with the finger extended); with r = 0.63 each extensor sends 37 % of its force to the central slip and 31.5 % to each lateral band. EDC2 and EIP share the index hood, so their IP arms are equal (1.9 / 2.6 mm).

IP moment arms stay extensor over the full PIP (0-115 deg) and DIP ranges for every branched tendon; the bands wrap a 1.9 mm cylinder on the PIP axis (Garcia-Elias 1991a). LU_RB5 no longer turns into a PIP flexor near 114-115 deg (S1b note).

Intrinsics (Chao & An coefficients): the first palmar interosseous matches (DIP 1.0 mm vs An 1.6, Lee 0.9); the lumbrical's 2/3 terminal share gives DIP 2.1 mm, 3-4x An 1983's 0.7 +- 0.6 and Lee 2008b's 0.53 mm (open check).

ORL: 23.7 % of the passive DIP resistance at PIP 0 (Ueba 25 %); slack at PIP 30-90 deg, where Ueba measured 31 / 18 / 3 %, because Harris & Rutledge's slack range (no force while DIP - PIP <= 30 deg) is kept as the constraint (Ueba's PIP 30 deg posture differs by 15 deg).

Intrinsic-plus: from the fist the index intrinsics reach MCP 92, PIP -1, DIP -1 deg in both models: the passive extensor tension (refitted since the proposal's prototype) already extended the DIP in S4. IP coupling under FDP2 alone: dDIP/dPIP 0.38 at PIP 70 deg (S4 0.52; Leijnse 1.0 +- 0.31); the ramp stalls at PIP 99 deg, so no slope at 100 deg.

Refits: extrinsic joint fit error 16211 -> 12271 (without the release step 7178 -> 1194), and test_joint_fit_matches_the_recorded_error passes again; the release bound of EDC3-5 and EDM rises from fpmax 0.0525 to 0.133 (smaller IP arms need more passive force to open the digits); every spring fit RMS is equal or smaller (digit-5 PIP 0.049 -> 0.022 N m).

Tenodesis passes; mean PIP range 19.7 -> 10.9 deg and the index-to-other-digit spread 70 / 37 -> 41 / 8 deg (ARMS 16.1 deg and 49 / 15 deg). Grip 377 -> 390 N, settled 340 -> 363 N; lateral pinch 52.9 -> 53.1 N.

steps.title: S5: interossei and lumbricals by identity
steps.summary: The finger-side bundles RI3-5, LU_RB2-5 and UI_UB2-4 become the anatomical muscles PI1-3, DI2-4 and LUM1-4 (same actuator indices): Jacobson 1992 architecture at 86.3 N/cm2; PI1-3 and the lumbricals end on a band junction of the extensor mechanism, DI2-4 split into a bony branch and a hood branch with Salsbury 1937's shares (DI2 0.48, DI3 0.93, DI4 0.66); paths fitted to An 1983 (index) and An 1979 (digits 3-5); lumbrical band fractions fitted to An 1983's IP arms (central 0.368, band 0.228). Intrinsic passive scales, extrinsic slack lengths and passive scales, and joint springs refitted. Before = EM-a; the before columns of the new muscles are the bundles they replace, measured on the EM-a model.
notes: MCP moment arms after the fit (flexion / abduction, mm): every muscle within the 2 mm tolerance of An 1979 or one SD of An 1983 except DI2's flexion arm (5.5 against 10.2 mm; the fibre-length window, 0.5 at full MCP extension, holds its sites) and PI3's abduction arm (8.5 against 10.0 mm). The old bundles had the wrong side for DI3, DI4 and PI3 only in name, but their MCP arms were 1/3 to 1/2 of the targets (e.g. LU_RB3 flexion 3.0 against 13.4 mm).

Forces: the lumbricals fall from 48-98 N to 5.2-9.5 N (Jacobson PCSA 0.06-0.11 cm2), the interossei change to 52.6-115.6 N. Ketchum et al. 1978's in-vivo nerve-block estimates for the index (a weak check) are DI1 53 +- 25, first palmar interosseous 27 +- 12 and first lumbrical 20 +- 9 N; the model has 129, 65 and 9.5 N at 86.3 N/cm2.

Lumbrical band fractions: Chao & An's 2/3 terminal share gave LUM1 a DIP arm of 2.1 mm; fitted to An 1983 it is 0.70 / 1.80 mm (DIP / PIP) with central 0.368, band 0.228 and 0.405 on the proximal phalanx. At Lee 2008b's postures 0.77 / 2.03 mm (Lee: 0.53 / -0.84). The interossei keep Chao & An (PI1 1.0 / 1.9 mm, between An 1.6 / 2.6 and Lee 0.9 / 0.13). With the weaker lumbricals the FDP-alone coupling slope at PIP 70 deg falls from 0.38 to 0.26 (Leijnse 1.0 +- 0.31).
Hood fractions (decision D6 pending): replacing DI2-4's Salsbury shares by 0.5 each changes the grip by -1 % and the digit shares by at most 0.8 points.

Refits: intrinsic passive scales (thumb rows: OP 0.0035 -> 0.0065, APB 0.44 -> 0.58; PI3 and LUM4 stay at the class value 1.3), extrinsic joint-fit error 12271 -> 10569 (without release 1194 -> 1020; release bound of EDC3-5/EDM 0.133 -> 0.125), springs refitted.

Grip 390 -> 335 N, settled 363 -> 267 N; digit-3 share 33.0 -> 29.7 %, 0.5 points outside the protocol's 12-point band around ARMS's 42.2 % (test_grip_at_the_cached_optimum fails; the grip keeps every finger intrinsic at full activation, and the middle finger loses LU_RB3's 98 N MCP flexion). Tenodesis passes with a mean PIP range of 16.1 deg (ARMS 16.1); lateral pinch 53.1 -> 51.5 N.

steps.title: S6: lumbrical junction nodes
steps.summary: Each lumbrical arises from a junction node on its own FDP tendon: a light body on a slide joint (node_LUM1-4_r) in the metacarpal, on the FDP path at the S5 origin level, tied by a tendon equality to the FDP path distal of the node (s = L_distal(q) - L_distal(q0); rigid tendon), the forward-dynamics form of Engelhardt et al. 2021's substitute segment. Node armature 0.03 kg, damping 5 N s/m, equality solref 0.004 1 (numerical). Lumbrical slack length at the middle of its excursion; own moment arms unchanged; passive scales, extrinsic passive fit and springs refitted. Before = S5.
notes: Lumbrical excursion from the straight finger to the flexion limits: 31.9 / 36.7 / 36.5 / 29.6 mm (LUM1-4; a fixed origin shortened them by 0-10 mm); Ranney & Wells 1988 measured 25 -> 56 mm (+31 mm) on index fingers. With the node following its FDP, LUM1's MCP flexion dL/dq at rest is +3.0 mm (a slight extensor; An 1983's FP minus LU arm gives +1.8 +- 2.4 mm), PIP +6.8 and DIP +4.3 mm (extensor): the small MCP and large IP terms of Leijnse & Kalker 1995.

LUM1 alone (1 s, from rest): MCP2 25 deg flexion with PIP and DIP at 0 (S5's fixed origin: 82 deg); the tie residual stays below 0.3 mm in a fist and 0.5 mm with FDP2 and LUM1 active; no force chatter at 2 ms (0.002 N step to step; the prototype's 1e-2 kg without damping chattered by 2.8 N). Index joint error against a 0.1 ms run over a fist / lumbricals / release protocol: 0.53 deg RMS, 1.6 deg max (S5: 0.67 / 2.7 deg).

Grip 335 -> 332 N (settled 267 -> 263 N), middle-finger share 29.7 -> 27.9 % (test_grip_at_the_cached_optimum still fails, now 2.3 points outside); tenodesis passes; lateral pinch unchanged (51.5 N). The lumbricals now carry 4-7 N of passive tension at the flexion limits (1.32-1.36 L_fo).

steps.title: S7: juncturae tendinum, FCU, FDS5
steps.summary: Junction nodes on EDC3, EDC4 and EDC5 with tension-only junctura links EDC4-EDC3 and EDC4-EDC5, stiffness fitted to von Schroeder & Botte 1993's traction transfers; FCU over the pisiform (via point fitted to Horii 1993) and the hamate hook to the MC5 base; FDS5 force from Holzbaur 2005 scaled like FDS2-4 (75.3 -> 46.5 N); extrinsic slack lengths, passive scales and springs refitted. ECU's forearm-rotation dependence and the FDP inter-tendon links were tried or considered and not added (hand-extrinsic-muscles.md). Before = S6.
notes: Juncturae: ring-finger traction extends the little-finger MP by 22.3 deg more with the links (von Schroeder & Botte: 22 deg junctura share), the middle-finger MP by 6.2 deg (18 deg): JT34 sits at its upper stiffness bound (1000 N/m, set by force chatter at 2 ms), and even a rigid link stays far below because of its obliquity. Middle-finger traction does not reach the neighbours (7-8 deg in the cadavers): a tension-only link from the ring tendon slackens.

FCU: flexion / ulnar arms 18.4 / 10.6 -> 14.7 / 12.2 mm (Horii 16 +- 3 / 14 +- 3), unchanged with forearm rotation; CMC5 flexion arm 4.6 -> 3.1 mm. ECU unchanged: 7.5 mm extension at every forearm rotation against Loren's 7.8 / 7.2 / 0.9 mm (supination / neutral / pronation); with its groove on the ulna the model's rotation axis, about 20 mm from the groove, swings the arm from 16 to -12.6 mm.

Extrinsic passive refit: joint-fit error 10812 -> 1754 (without the release step 1020 -> 1017); the release bound of EDC3-5 and EDM fpmax falls 0.127 -> 0.028, since the juncturae carry part of the ring and little fingers' opening. Springs: digit-5 CMC RMS 0.005 -> 0.023 N m (peak 0.96 N m), the other rows within 0.001 N m.
Grip 331.5 -> 324.6 N, middle-finger share 27.9 -> 25.2 % (protocol band 42.2 +- 12, already outside since S5). Tenodesis passes (mean PIP range 16.0 -> 14.5 deg); lateral pinch unchanged (51.5 N).

Springs refitted a second time after the junctura fit's second pass (digit-5 CMC RMS 0.023 N m); the hand-function values are from the model before that refit (spring change below 0.004 N m), the geometric values from the final model.

steps.title: EDC2 wrist wrap: side site dorsal of its sphere
steps.summary: EDC2's wrist-wrap side site moves from the centre of its sphere (inside wrap: the tendon held within the sphere's circle, solved differently by MuJoCo and mujoco-warp) to the sphere's dorsal side (ordinary wrap over the dorsal surface, as over the carpus); the sphere is unchanged. Extrinsic slack lengths and passive scales, the junctura links and the springs refitted. Before = S7.
notes: EDC2: wrist extension arm 17.3 -> 18.7 mm at neutral (20.2 -> 24.0 mm at 60 deg extension, 6.2 -> 9.5 mm at 60 deg flexion), ulnar-deviation arm 2.3 -> 4.9 mm; finger arms unchanged (the wrap spans the wrist only), so the An 1983 / Lee 2008b rows do not move. CPU and mujoco-warp EDC2 lengths agree within 1e-6 m in 512 random arm postures (0.79 mm before).

Extrinsic passive refit: joint-fit error 1754 -> 959 (without the release step 1017 -> 727); index (Knutson) RMSE 3.35 -> 3.49 N cm; EDC2 fpmax 0.62 -> 0.18, release bound of EDC3-5 and EDM 0.028 -> 0.0285. Springs: wrist deviation RMS 0.070 -> 0.044 N m, thumb CMC flexion 0.076 -> 0.008 N m, digit-5 CMC 0.023 -> 0.019 N m, the other rows within 0.002 N m.

Junctura refit on the refitted model: JT34 999.9 -> 993 N/m (still at its bound), JT45 263 -> 222 N/m; ring-finger traction moves the middle finger 13.8 deg without links (27.0 before, contact-driven), so the junctura share rises to the value in the table.
Grip 324.6 -> 345.0 N (settled 251.6 -> 256.1 N), middle-finger share 25.2 -> 24.8 %; tenodesis passes (mean MCP 65.1, PIP 14.2 deg); lateral pinch 51.5 -> 53.1 N (thumb passive terms refitted).

steps.title: Shared terminal tendon of the lateral bands (step time)
steps.summary: The extensors' two lateral-band branches end where the bands converge, and their common terminal tendon (convergence site -> DIP wrap -> terminal insertion) is one pulley branch carrying both band fractions: the same tendon lengths and moment arms (to 1e-16 m), the terminal wrap computed once. No parameter changes. Before = EDC2 wrap.
notes: Equivalence against the EDC2-wrap model: actuator lengths within 1.1e-16 m, moment arms within 3.5e-18 m, joint accelerations within 4e-15 (relative) in 100 random postures of myohand_r, myoarms and myofullbody. Tenodesis, the self-selected grip and the pinch are identical; the neutral-wrist grip re-optimisation lands in another local optimum (245.6 -> 233.0 N, posture change -29 -> -32 %), a sensitivity of the optimiser to roundoff, not of the model.

CPU step time (one thread, interleaved A/B, best of 4): myohand_r -0.9 %, myohands -0.8 %, myoarm_r -2.2 %, myoarms -1.4 %, myofullbody -1.8 %; kinematics plus tendons -0.8 / -2.6 / -5.6 us in myohand_r / myoarms / myofullbody.

steps.title: JT3/JT5 node ties from EDC-P4
steps.summary: The tie helpers of the junctura nodes start at the EDC's via point EDC{d}-P4_r, proximal of the node, instead of the node's rest point near the MC head, so they take the EDC's MCP wrap and every node moves with its tendon over the MCP range (within 1e-6 m; the JT3 and JT5 nodes moved 6-11 mm too far at MCP 90 deg). The links are slack up to the longer of their lengths with straight fingers and in the resting posture. Junctura links, extrinsic passive fit and springs refitted. Before = shared terminal tendon.
notes: Node vs tendon excursion over the MCP range (IPs straight and at the resting posture): within 1e-6 m for JT3-5; the S7 helper (from the rest point) as negative control gives 6-11 mm at MCP 90 deg (JT3 22.3 vs 12.3 mm, JT5 19.5 vs 9.0 mm). JT4 and the lumbrical nodes were already exact.

Junctura refit: JT34 993 -> 1000 N/m, JT45 221.9 -> 1000 N/m (both at the numerical bound); ring-finger traction extends the middle / little MP by 17.0 / 21.6 deg more with the links (von Schroeder & Botte 1993: 18 / 22; before 17.1 / 21.7). JT45's rest length is now its straight-finger length (1.1 mm longer than in the resting posture).

Extrinsic passive refit: joint-fit error 959 -> 1127 (without the release step 727 -> 722); release bound of EDC3-5 and EDM 0.0285 -> 0.0377. Springs: digit-4 / digit-5 CMC RMS 0.001 / 0.019 -> 0.013 / 0.045 N m (the stiffer EDC4-EDC5 link acts between MC4 and MC5); other rows within 0.002 N m.

Grip 345.0 -> 328.0 N (settled 256.1 -> 266.5 N), middle-finger share 24.8 -> 29.6 %; tenodesis passes (mean MCP 67.0, PIP 13.9 deg); lateral pinch 53.1 -> 53.2 N. CPU step unchanged within noise (myohand_r 63.2 -> 63.8, myoarms 240.2 -> 238.4, myofullbody 488.0 -> 470.2 us).

steps.title: S2c: AdPt insertion and APL CMC routing after Barry et al. 2018
steps.summary: Barry et al. 2018's OpenSim thumb model (2020 revision; MyoHand's bone meshes and frames) supplies the AdPt insertion on the proximal phalanx (with Mirakhorlo 2016's transverse-head fibre length, 40.8 mm, inside the 1.6 L_fo window) and APL's CMC routing: from its MC1-base via point over a trapezium cylinder (Barry's THM_CMC1_APL ellipsoid as a cylinder) to Barry's MC1-base insertion. Barry's FPL CMC routing reaches Smutz's flexion arm but makes the lateral pinch infeasible and is not used. Thumb passive scales, extrinsic slack lengths and passive scales, junctura links and springs refitted. Before = JT3/JT5 ties.
notes: Smutz 1998 neutral (mm, + = flexor / adductor): AdPt CMC flexion / abduction / MP flexion 19.4 / 16.8 / 2.6 -> 21.6 / 18.9 / 6.9 (Smutz 36.9 / 20.6 / 9.7; RMS z over 3 postures per joint 1.90 -> 1.74); APL CMC flexion / abduction 1.4 / -2.6 -> -7.1 / -11.3 (Smutz -7.1 / -10.5; RMS z 2.34 -> 0.71); FPL unchanged 4.2 / -1.7 / 7.1 (Smutz 14.3 / -0.2 / 13.6). AdPt fibre length over the full ranges 0.12-1.60 L_fo (window 1.6). APL's wrist arms unchanged.

Not adopted: Barry's FPL CMC routing (trapezium point and first MC1 point; CMC flexion arm 14.3 mm, RMS z 2.50 -> 1.70) and the trapezium point alone (13.8 mm): the lateral pinch has no solution within its off-axis limit (best 3.6 N). Barry's AdPo path likewise (earlier trial).

Refits: thumb passive scales (cost 6274 -> 5907; AdPt 0.69 -> 0.89, APB 0.56 -> 0.54), extrinsic slack lengths and passive scales (joint-fit error 1127 -> 1050, without the release step 722 -> 672; APL slack +7.2 %, fpmax 1.3 -> 0.29; release bound 0.0377 -> 0.0391), junctura links (JT45 1000 -> 997.8 N/m), springs (thumb CMC flexion RMS 0.008 -> 0.015, CMC abduction 0.076 -> 0.081 N m).

Lateral pinch 53.2 -> 67.5 N (in vivo 51.9 +- 20.4 N; off-axis 0.17), now with APL 0.46, OP 0.32 and APB 0.81 active; grip 328.0 -> 330.7 N (middle-finger share 29.6 -> 29.2 %); tenodesis passes. CPU and mujoco-warp agree on APL and AdPt (random wrist and thumb postures). CPU step within noise.
